title: The Purpose of Trials and the Victory over the Dragon
english: … practised), but “that you might be made manifest.” Let us not be shown to be unjust, or ungodly. Let us remember these things in times of hardship, and let us think that we hear God, present with us and saying to us: “Do you think that I have dealt with you for any other reason than that your righteousness might become plain to those who do not know it?”

“Take up now loftiness and power, and clothe yourself in glory and honour” (Job 40:10). Crown yourself: put on glory, put on honour, put on comeliness. The insolent one made war on you, but you humbled the proud one and turned his ranks back far away in shame. Convict sinners by showing them to be sinners; fill their faces with dishonour through the proof that is in you. So it is not for display; or else it is for all the other things as well, or even for the knowledge of God. See how far he convicts Job of the lowliness of his nature: he does not say that you are lowly, but that I am great, and that he cannot do what I can.

“But now, behold, wild beasts are with you” (Job 40:15). As an athlete, learn about the dragon, your opponent. With you, then, he says, and with everyone who endures, these beasts are tamed and made subject. There is, however … and so on.

“Will you lead a dragon with a hook, and put a halter round his nose?” (Job 41:1). Can you, then, he says, O Job, do what the Only-begotten later accomplished? For he held out his own flesh to him as a kind of bait, and through his own nails, as through hooks, he caught the fish Leviathan. That is what the Hebrew has, and it means the dragon.

“Will you lay a hand on him, remembering the war that is waged in his body? And let it happen no more” (Job 41:8). By war he means here the turmoil, the savagery, his onrush. How can that be done? he says. Such is the beast: savage and powerful and senseless. Can you, he says, bind him down by your own strength? Or even so much as remember and conceive the war that is to be waged in his body? By his body he means the demons, since he is their head; and this war the Lord won through the trophy of the cross. And “let it happen no more” is said because the cross has taken place once; for “he who died to sin,” it says, “died once for all” (Romans 6:10).
“Who will uncover the face of his garment?” (Job 41:13).

added_allusions.reason: God's question 'Do you think that I have dealt with you ... that your righteousness might become plain' recasts the LXX of Job 40:8 ('that you might appear righteous'); the wording is changed, so no reference is printed.
'The insolent one ... you humbled the proud one' paraphrases the commands about the proud in Job 40:11-12; a paraphrase, not cited inline.

'Fill their faces with dishonour' matches the Septuagint wording of Psalm 82:17 LXX (KJV Psalm 83:16 'Fill their faces with shame'); the LXX of Job 40:13 has a similar phrase. Which text is echoed is uncertain, so it is not cited inline.

translator_notes: Copy-text: PG 12; Homiliae in Job (Khazarzar) locked Greek in translations/*_source.json.
Pass A is a literal sense gloss; Pass B is literary English constrained by A.
Khazarzar research-footer lines stripped; Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

2026-11-11 (round 2): checked clause by clause against the locked Greek and retranslated; the old English misread δόξωμεν as 'glory' ('hearing the glory of God'), turned 'let us not be shown unjust' into an address to Job, made the lowly nature the subject that rebukes (God convicts Job of it) and reversed 'he cannot do what I can', rendered 'wild beasts are with you' as 'set against you', made Leviathan the fisher ('so did Leviathan draw up the dragon', 'ribs' for nails) where the Only-begotten catches Leviathan, and read 'since he is their head' as 'as if they were his head'. The lemmas now carry English verse numbers from the catena labels (εʹ, ιʹ, κʹ, κζʹ, ΜΑʹ δʹ = LXX Job 40:5, 40:10, 40:20, 40:27, 41:4 = KJV 40:10, 40:15, 41:1, 41:8, 41:13). The display 'Romans 6:10' was linked to Hebrews 9:28; it is now the plain reference Romans 6:10. The closing article Τὸ belongs to the first sentence of u03-rem-early.
